Hi! I'm completely new to this and don't know where to start, can you guide me?

Agent response: It's great that you're curious about starting a plant-based journey! Many people are interested in adding more plants to their diet for health and sustainability reasons, and we're here to help guide you. First, it's helpful to know that a plant-based diet is an umbrella term. It doesn't always mean you have to go fully vegan or vegetarian right away. It simply means consciously choosing foods from plant sources, making them the primary focus of your diet. This can include: Plant-forward or Flexitarian: Mostly plants, but occasionally consuming animal products. Vegetarian: No meat, but may include eggs and dairy. Vegan: No meat, eggs, dairy, and sometimes no honey. Raw Vegan: Foods are dehydrated, lightly steamed, or eaten raw to preserve enzymes. The key is to focus on getting the right amounts of both macro- and micronutrients. A plant-based diet isn't automatically healthy; it requires attention to nutrition. If you're just starting, here are some baby steps you can take: Focus on Plant Sources: Consciously choose foods from plant sources. Adjust Portion Sizes: Consider making animal products a side dish and increasing the amount of vegetables, grains, or healthy fats in your meals. Incorporate Plant-Based Proteins: To ensure you're getting enough protein, add sources like beans, lentils, edamame, tofu, tempeh, and quinoa to your meals. You can learn more about getting started with a plant-based diet here: The Beginner’s Guide To A Plant Based Diet and Baby Steps to Trying a Plant-Based Diet (And Enjoying it). Is there anything else a beginner needs to get started?

Agent response: That's a great question! Beyond choosing your first Soylent product, there are a few practical things a beginner might find helpful to know to get started smoothly: 1. Preparation: If you opt for Soylent powder, preparation is simple. Our favorite way to get the best taste and texture is using a blender and chilling for 20 minutes before enjoying it, but a shaker bottle works really well too! Mixing Ratios: For an 8oz serving, mix ½ cup (60g) of Soylent with 1 cup of water. For a 12oz serving, mix ⅔ cup (90g) of Soylent with 1½ cup of water. Each scoop of powder is approximately ⅓ cup, but for exact measurements, using a scale is recommended. Enjoy: Prepare with ice or chill before serving. Storage (Mixed): Store any unfinished, mixed Soylent in the fridge and consume within two days. 2. How to Incorporate Soylent into Your Diet: While Soylent can replace any meal, it is not intended to replace every meal. If you are just getting started, we recommend incorporating Soylent gradually into a balanced diet. Many people find success replacing a few meals a week, often starting with breakfasts, or keeping a few bottles on hand for when life gets busy. Soylent can help you reach your nutrition goals over the course of a day or week. It's designed to be an antidote for the 'food void' – those times when you're stuck without access to a good, quality meal, saving you from less nutritious options. 3. Storage (Unopened): Unopened Soylent can be stored at room temperature with a shelf-life of up to one year. While most users choose to refrigerate their Soylent before enjoying it, it isn’t required. Heat should not cause Soylent to spoil, but if temperatures go above 110 degrees, the vitamins & nutrients may begin to break down over time. 4. Consult a Professional: As with any change in diet or health, we recommend talking to your health care provider or nutritionist to determine if Soylent is a good fit for your specific needs. You can find more details on preparation and usage in our FAQs on the Meal Replacement Powders page and in the Getting Started section of our FAQ.
